topic_en: Rust: Move vs Clone vs Copy

xhs.title: let b = a 之后，a 为啥不能用了？
xhs.body:
第 7 课：Move、Clone、Copy
Move：所有权搬走，旧变量作废
Clone：手动 .clone()，完整复制一份，可能很贵
Copy：i32 这类只在栈上的类型，赋值自动复制，旧的照样能用
考考你：let a = 5; let b = a; 之后再打印 a，能编译吗？ 评论区告诉我～

linkedin.title: Move, Clone, Copy: three ways a Rust value gets passed on
linkedin.body:
Move: ownership goes to the new variable; the old one can't be used.
Clone: an explicit .clone() that copies heap data in full, and can be costly.
Copy: stack-only types like i32 are copied automatically, and the old variable still works.
Under the hood, Move and Copy both copy bytes. The difference is whether the old variable stays valid.
Quick quiz: let a = 5; let b = a; then print a. Does it compile? Answer in the comments.

quiz.q_zh: let a = 5; let b = a; 之后再打印 a，能编译吗？
quiz.q_en: let a = 5; let b = a; then print a. Does it compile?
quiz.answer_zh: 答案：能！i32 是 Copy 类型，赋值是复制一份，a 照样能用。换成 String 就不行了。
quiz.answer_en: Answer: yes! i32 is Copy, so the assignment copies the value and a still works. With a String it would not.
